Subject: Batching & caching roadmap for AtlasAI onboarding

Pete —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Per our conversation I've sketched a pragmatic onboarding plan focused on unlocking cost savings while protecting latency for your customer-facing features. High level asks below; attached is a short economics snapshot I put together (atlas_initial_econ_snapshot.pdf).

Key asks from AtlasAI before kickoff:
- 1 week of representative request traces (JSON lines, anonymized) or a summary: queries/sec, average prompt tokens, 95th token length.
- Target SLOs by route (e.g., chat: p95 < 250 ms; batch infer: throughput X qps).
- Any hard constraints (no model quantization due to regulatory reasons).

Initial Redwood tuning proposals (pre-kickoff):
- Batching baseline: establish dynamic batching with 20–50 ms max-wait window for interactive routes.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated context (we'll attach cache hit rate targets).
- Quantization profile candidates: 4-bit LLMQ and 8-bit fallback; we'll test output delta vs your prompt set.
- Routing: route high-MLU (long-history) requests to deduped cache pools; fallback to lower-cost quantized endpoints when latency budget allows.

Next steps I propose:
1) You share sample traces + SLA spreadsheet (we can take the spreadsheet you mentioned).
2) Internal kickoff this Monday to align owners + run a 2h benchmark (engine + infra).
3) Redwood sends quant profile matrix and small test harness (we'll coordinate quotas).

I'll be on PTO Thurs–Fri but available for Monday kickoff.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Appreciate the clear plan. Attaching our SLA sheet (atlas_sla_requirements.xlsx). A few notes to help prioritize:
- Traffic profile: steady-state 8–12 qps during business hours; spikes to ~75 qps for short periods (30–90s) during product launches.
- Typical prompt tokens: 120 tokens (user) + 600 tokens (context) for chat routes; embedding calls smaller but frequent.
- Hard constraint: procurement requires separate proof-of-compliance for any on-prem changes (we can provide contacts).

Procurement (cc'd) will handle contract milestones; feel free to loop in legal. We'll upload anonymized traces by EOD tomorrow.

Looping in some quick technical guidance so the kickoff is productive.

Olga / team —
- Quantization: given the ~720 token context on chat routes, we should test 4-bit LLMQ first for low-cost baselines. We'll keep an 8-bit fallback for any observed quality regression (>2% dev metric drop). I attached a small CSV of candidate profiles and expected latency deltas (redwood_quant_profiles.csv).
- Batching window: dynamic with adaptive sizing. For interactive routes aim to cap window at 30 ms; for background batch jobs we can go up to 150 ms to maximize throughput.
- Cache policy: configure prefix cache TTL at 45 min for session-type workloads; set a cold-start warmup to pre-populate top 5% of prefixes seen in the trace.
- Routing policy: tag requests by 'route_tier' (interactive|background|embedding) and route interactive -> low-latency pool; background -> high-batch pool. We should also provision a small reserved pool for launch spikes (burst capacity).

I'll prepare a short benchmark plan (latency histogram targets + artifact collection) and post it to the Drive link. If procurement needs a compliance worksheet for quantized endpoints, Ben can take point.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
